name: native-text
description: Typography primitive for React Native. Every string on screen must live inside a Text; this one carries the theme's foreground colour, a typographic variant scale, and inherits classes from styled parents (Button, Card, Badge) through TextClassContext.

props.name: variant
props.description: Typographic role — headings, body, lead, small, muted, code

props.name: className
props.description: Additional NativeWind classes; wins over both the variant and any inherited parent classes

props.name: numberOfLines
props.description: Truncate to this many lines with an ellipsis (React Native Text prop)

props.name: selectable
props.description: Let the user long-press to select and copy the text

values.description: Card or group heading (2xl, semibold); announced as a heading

values.description: Minor heading (xl, semibold); announced as a heading
values.useWhen: sub-groups within a card or settings section
multi-line prose such as descriptions, empty-state copy, onboarding text
the one-sentence subtitle under a screen title
a key figure or emphasised value (a balance, a count)

values.description: Small medium-weight label with tight line height

values.description: Small text in the muted foreground colour
values.useWhen: helper text, secondary descriptions, placeholders rendered as text

values.description: Inline code chip on the muted background
values.useWhen: an identifier, command or token the user might copy

ai.whenToUse: Use for every string rendered in a React Native screen. Reach for a heading variant (h1–h4) for titles so screen readers announce them, 'muted' or 'small' for secondary copy, and the default variant everywhere else.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't render text outside a Text — React Native throws when a bare string is a child of a View. Don't use it for editable content (use Input or Textarea). Don't stack many variants to build a layout; wrap Text elements in a View with gap classes instead.
commonMistakes: Importing Text from react-native directly — the raw element ignores the theme foreground colour and the class inheritance parents rely on, so a Button label renders in default black on a dark button
Passing a bare string as a Button or Card child instead of wrapping it in Text — React Native throws 'Text strings must be rendered within a <Text> component'
Putting a View inside a Text to build a layout — nest Text inside Text for mixed styling, but use a View container for anything positional
Reaching for h1 more than once per screen — VoiceOver users navigate by heading, and several h1s flatten the hierarchy
ai.accessibilityNotes: Heading variants (h1–h4) set role="heading" so VoiceOver and TalkBack announce them and users can jump between them; React Native has no aria-level, so the hierarchy comes from reading order. Body text has no role. Keep contrast by using the foreground and muted-foreground tokens rather than custom colours; both are audited in light and dark.
